description: client_billing_profiles table exists with PK (tenant, billing_profile_id), FK to clients, and name/is_default/is_active columns.

Exactly one default profile per client is enforced at the database layer: a partial unique index rejects a second default (at-most-one), and a deferred constraint trigger rejects any committed state where a client has profiles but no default (at-least-one).
is_system_managed_default marks backfilled profiles, following the system-managed default contract precedent.
Backfill creates exactly one default profile for every existing client, named from the client.
Backfill is idempotent and safe to re-run without creating duplicate profiles.
client_contracts gains a nullable billing_profile_id column.
contract_lines gains a nullable billing_profile_id column.
client_locations gains a nullable default_billing_profile_id column.
tickets gains a nullable billing_profile_id column.
projects gains a nullable billing_profile_id column.
invoice_charges gains billing_profile_id and billing_profile_source columns.
time_entries gains a contract_line_source column.
client_billing_profiles is registered in tenant table metadata so Citus distributes it correctly.
client_billing_profiles is included in the tenant deletion activity so tenant teardown removes it.
All phase-1 migrations have working down migrations that restore the prior schema.
A pure resolveChargeProfile function implements the five-step resolution chain.
The resolver returns a source value identifying which chain step produced the profile.
The resolver always terminates at the client default profile and never returns null.
A contract-line profile assignment takes precedence over a work-item profile assignment.
A contract profile assignment takes precedence over a work-item profile assignment.
An explicit profile on the source record takes precedence over every other step.
The time-entry billing query selects the ticket billing profile from the existing tickets join.
The time-entry billing query selects the project billing profile via the existing project joins.
Time-based charge computation stamps the resolved billing profile and source on each charge.
Usage-based charge computation stamps the resolved billing profile and source on each charge.
Fixed charge computation stamps the resolved billing profile and source at all of its stamp sites.
Bucket charge computation stamps the resolved billing profile and source on each charge.
Recurring-quantity charge computation stamps the resolved billing profile and source on each charge.
Invoice charge persistence writes billing_profile_id and billing_profile_source to invoice_charges.
Project schedule charge persistence stamps a billing profile, closing a path that currently stamps no segment at all.
Manual and ad-hoc invoice items accept and persist an explicit billing profile.
The sales-order invoicing path stamps a billing profile on generated charges.
The invoice modification path stamps a billing profile on generated charges.
Invoice totals and tax figures are unchanged for clients with a single billing profile.
A billing profiles section on the client detail page lists the client's profiles.
A user can create a billing profile under a client.
A user can rename a billing profile.
A user can archive a billing profile, removing it from pickers without deleting history.
A user can change which profile is the client's default.
Archiving the client's default profile is rejected with a clear message.
Deleting a profile that has charges is rejected and archiving is offered instead.
A useClientBillingProfiles hook returns the client's profiles and an isSegmented flag.
All billing profile UI is hidden on every surface while a client has exactly one profile.
A billing profile picker is available on a contract.
A billing profile picker is available on a contract line.
A location can be given a default billing profile.
A billing profile picker is available on a ticket.
A billing profile picker is available on a project.
A ticket's billing profile soft-defaults at creation from the location default, then the client default.
Ticket creation is never blocked by a missing or ambiguous billing profile.
A billing profile assigned to a ticket is validated to belong to the ticket's client.
Profile assignment changes are recorded with actor and timestamp on the affected record.
A spend-by-profile report shows total spend per profile over a selected period.
A user can drill from a profile total into the individual charges behind it.
The report supports comparing two periods.
The report can be exported.
The report reads from invoice_charges directly with no separate rollup table.
The spend-by-profile report is not offered for single-profile clients.
Charges that resolved via the client-default fallback are distinguishable in the report.
Access to the spend-by-profile report is governed by an RBAC permission.
billing_profile_source records which chain step won, across explicit, contract line, contract, work item, and client default.
contract_line_source records how a time entry's contract line was chosen, including the unresolved case.
contract_line_source is set when a time entry is created or updated.
contract_line_source is set when the generation-time reconcile path assigns a contract line.
An attribution inspector on an invoice line explains why the charge was attributed to its profile.
An attribution inspector on a time entry explains how its contract line was chosen.
Each source value renders a plain-language explanation sentence rather than a raw enum.
A queue lists time entries whose contract line could not be resolved because a service matched more than one line.
A user can resolve a queued entry by assigning a contract line to it.
The inspector states the contract-line granularity limitation for usage, bucket, fixed, and project-schedule charges.
The client portal shows organization-wide spend across all of a client's profiles.
A segment selector appears in the portal when the client has more than one profile.
A portal user can drill into spend for a single profile.
A portal user can view invoices filtered to a single profile.
A portal user can view tickets filtered to a single profile.
A portal user can view services and contracts filtered to a single profile.
The portal is visually and functionally identical to today for single-profile clients.
Portal segment views respect existing client portal RBAC and tenant scoping.
client_billing_profiles gains a bills_separately flag defaulting to false.
A profile can carry its own bill-to name.
A profile can carry its own bill-to location reference.
A profile can carry its own billing contact and invoice recipient.
A billing profile can carry its own tax exemption status and exemption certificate, falling back to the client when unset.
A profile can carry its own PO number and PO-required setting.
A profile can carry its own invoice delivery preferences.
A profile can carry its own billing cycle frequency overriding the client's.
Every profile-level billing field falls back to the client value when unset.
A UI lets a user edit a profile's bill-to identity, tax, PO, and delivery settings.
The tax region resolution chain is unchanged - service region, then contract-line location region, then client default - and a billing profile does not participate in it.
client_billing_cycles gains a non-null billing_profile_id column.
Existing billing cycle rows are backfilled to their client's default profile.
A unique constraint covers tenant, client, billing profile, and period start.
Billing cycle creation generates one cycle per separately-billing profile per period.
Invoice generation scopes charges to the profile of the cycle being generated.
A generated invoice reads bill-to details from its profile, falling back to the client.
invoices gains a billing_profile_id column identifying the profile it bills.
A profile's own billing cycle frequency is honored when generating its cycles.
The mixed-currency guard operates per profile rather than per client.
All non-test consumers of client_billing_cycles are updated for the new profile dimension.
A shared test fixture helper supplies a default billing profile so existing billing tests need only mechanical changes.
Per-profile cycle generation is gated behind a per-tenant feature flag.
payment_methods gains a non-null billing_profile_id column.
Existing payment methods are backfilled to their client's default profile.
Default payment method uniqueness is scoped to tenant, client, and profile.
Payment method management UI is scoped to a billing profile.
Payment collection for an invoice uses the payment method of that invoice's profile.
transactions gains a billing_profile_id column.
credit_tracking gains a billing_profile_id column.
credit_allocations gains a billing_profile_id column.
Existing AR rows are backfilled to their client's default profile.
Credit application is constrained to invoices belonging to the issuing profile.
The derived credit balance query is profile-aware rather than client-aware.
Aging is computed and displayed per billing profile.
Statements are produced per billing profile.
Client-level AR views sum balances, aging, and credits across the client's profiles.
External entity mappings can address a billing profile as the Alga-side entity.
A client maps to a QuickBooks parent customer.
A separately-billing profile maps to a QuickBooks sub-customer referencing the client's parent customer.
A single-profile client continues to map to a plain QuickBooks customer with no sub-customer.
Customer sync creates and updates sub-customers for separately-billing profiles.
Invoice export targets the sub-customer corresponding to the invoice's profile.
The customer mapping UI displays and allows editing profile-level mappings.
A portal user's permitted billing profiles can be stored and defaults to all profiles.
A restricted portal user sees only their permitted segments in every portal view.
A restricted portal user's organization-wide totals reflect only their permitted segments.
An admin UI sets which profiles a portal user may see.
Profile restriction is enforced server-side on portal data queries, not only in the UI.

A golden-output baseline harness captures invoice totals, line amounts, tax figures, credit application, portal-visible output (portal invoice list and rendering view model), and accounting-export output including the customer/invoice identity fields the export maps (invoice number, client id, client name), and can diff a later run against it byte-for-byte. Baseline captured from the pre-S1 commit (parent of the S1 commit); provenance is independently re-derivable via baseline.provenance.json (pre-S1 SHA, tree hash, baseline sha256) plus verify-baseline-provenance.sh, which rebuilds a pre-S1 worktree, re-runs the capture, and byte-diffs against the committed baseline (T013).
prdRefs: Backward-compatibility gate (T013) — runs after every slice

description: A billing profile can carry its own tax ID number, falling back to the client when unset.
client_tax_settings is re-keyed to (tenant, client_id, billing_profile_id) so reverse-charge applicability is per profile, with existing rows backfilled to the client's default profile.
Charge tax context is built per resolved billing profile rather than per client, so a single invoice can carry both exempt and non-exempt lines.
Default tax settings provisioning creates a row for the resolved billing profile rather than only for the client.
Contract-line disambiguation accepts the resolved billing profile and, when more than one line is eligible, prefers the line whose contract belongs to that profile.
Profile-aware contract-line narrowing is applied when a time entry is created or updated.
Profile-aware contract-line narrowing is applied on the generation-time reconcile path.
Profile-aware narrowing that still leaves more than one candidate reports ambiguity rather than picking arbitrarily.

The existing unresolved rows in the billing dashboard show why an item is unresolved, distinguishing ambiguous from no-contract-covers-this-service, a distinction the engine computes today but only writes to logs.
An unresolved row offers inline remediation - assign a contract line - after which the item bills at contract pricing rather than catalog pricing.
An ambiguous item is never silently billed at service catalog default rate; falling back to catalog pricing becomes an explicit per-item choice by the biller.
An item with no eligible contract line continues to bill at service catalog default rate and is labelled as not covered by any contract.
Unresolved usage records receive the same reason surfacing, remediation, and explicit-fallback treatment as time entries.
The unresolved-item UI states that catalog pricing ignores contract rate, rounding, minimums, overtime, and pricing schedules.

Every client created after the S1 backfill also gets exactly one system-managed default billing profile: provisioned eagerly at each client-creation path and lazily by the resolution chain's terminal step, so no creation path can leave a client unattributable.
